known_limit.strict: open defect. 2/3 found, both named green. Strict's threshold lands above the third LED's core, so it never becomes a blob here. Normal and loose now get all three.

note: Five-port switch on a white wall in a dark corner, photographed with the camera's own auto exposure. Three green link LEDs in a diagonal row on the front edge, partly behind white ethernet cables; they blink quickly, so a single frame may miss one. An orange cable crosses above them and is the interesting negative - it is a reflector, and at loose it still gets a ring. WHAT WENT WRONG: two separate things, and only one of them was the exposure. The camera in a dark room opens up AND warms up - the greys in this frame come back R/G 1.12 against 0.95 in the lit capture - and that cast alone dragged the LED fringes to hue 75, 82 and 94: green, named YELLOW, with agreement over 0.99. Dividing the illuminant out before reading hue moves them to 94, 100 and 135, so the app now says GREEN, GREEN and YELLOW OR GREEN at loose. What is left is the exposure itself: the cores are still blown to [245,255,213], [234,255,196] and [236,255,223] at saturation around 0.2, and the lit capture reads 150 to 163 where this one reads 94 to 135. THEN: reading hue from the brightest 30% of each blob instead of its unclipped fringe moved all three to 124, 121 and 152 - GREEN at normal and loose, no hedging, and strict now finds two of the three instead of none. The exposure was never the fix; see 0003-dark-router, where the camera honoured the request and blacked the frame out entirely. This entry closes when strict finds the third LED too.
